en: The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and primarily inhabits the tropical forests of Mindanao.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white flower, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
The Philippine Congress, consisting of the Senate and the House of Representatives, holds the legislative power to make laws.
The Ifugao people built the magnificent Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera mountains over two thousand years ago.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a traditional two-steps-forward, one-step-back dance.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, with Filipino and English serving as the official national languages.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to help reduce infant mortality in rural Philippine areas without electricity.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The golden South Sea pearl, harvested from the Pinctada maxima oyster, was declared the national gem of the Philippines in 1996.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is historically demonstrated by neighbors carrying a nipa house to a new location.
The water buffalo, locally called the carabao, is the national animal and is essential for plowing Philippine rice fields.
